title: Turkey says it is applying the Montreux Convention to restrict warship passage through the Turkish Straits
body:
Within days of Russia's invasion of Ukraine, Turkey announced that it was applying the 1936 Montreux Convention, which gives Ankara control over the Dardanelles and Bosphorus straits. Under the convention, Turkey can limit the passage of warships in wartime or when it feels threatened. Foreign Minister Mevlut Cavusoglu, speaking on Sunday 27 February 2022, said: "We have alerted both countries of the region and elsewhere not to pass warships through the Black Sea."

Ukraine had asked Ankara to activate the convention and block Russian warships moving from the Mediterranean into the Black Sea. As a NATO member, Turkey had until that Sunday avoided calling the situation in Ukraine a war, a designation relevant to how the convention is applied. President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said: "We will not compromise our national interests." On the Monday that followed he called Russia's attack on Ukrainian territory "unacceptable" and urged good-faith negotiations.

Cavusoglu said Turkey had received no requests from any country for warships to pass through the straits since the war began. Al Jazeera reported that at least six Russian warships and a submarine had reportedly transited the straits earlier in the month, including the corvette Dmitry Rogachev, which passed through the Bosphorus on 16 February 2022. The convention also governs commercial shipping, which remains free in peacetime.
